Canada.text: Its provinces and territories reach three oceans: the Atlantic, the Pacific and the Arctic.
Canada.evidence: Its ten provinces and three territories extend from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean and northward into the Arctic Ocean, making it the second-largest country by total area, with the longest coastline of any country.

Norway.text: Its English name comes from the Old English Norþweg, "the way north", the sailing route along its coast.
Norway.evidence: The English name Norway comes from the Old English word Norþweg ... meaning "northern way" or "way leading to the north", which is how the Anglo-Saxons referred to the coastline of Atlantic Norway. ... the full name was Norðr vegr, "the way northwards", referring to the sailing route along the Norwegian coast

Indonesia.text: Between 13,000 and 17,000 islands make it the world's largest archipelagic state.
Indonesia.evidence: Comprising between 13,000 and 17,000 islands ... it is the world's largest archipelagic state and the 14th-largest country by area.

Russia.text: Its territory first reached the Black Sea coast in 1783, with the annexation of the Crimean Khanate.
Russia.evidence: Following the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774, Russian territory reached the coastline of the Black Sea, through its annexation of the Crimean Khanate in 1783.

Philippines.text: It consists of about 7,641 islands, grouped as Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao.
Philippines.evidence: Located in the western Pacific Ocean, it consists of about 7,641 islands ... The islands are broadly categorized into three main geographical divisions: from north to south, Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.

Japan.text: Besides its four major islands, its archipelago has over 14,000 smaller ones.
Japan.evidence: The Japanese archipelago consists of four major islands alongside over 14,000 smaller islands.

Australia.text: Its written history began with Dutch explorers charting most of its coastline in the 17th century.
Australia.evidence: Australia's written history commenced with Dutch exploration of most of the coastline in the 17th century.

United States.text: Its first people came from Siberia at least 15,000 years ago, maybe along an Ice Age coast now under the sea.
United States.evidence: The first inhabitants of North America migrated from Siberia at least 15,000 years ago, either across the Bering land bridge or along the now-submerged Ice Age coastline.

New Zealand.text: Its islands were the last large habitable land on Earth to be settled by humans.
New Zealand.evidence: The islands of New Zealand were the last large habitable land to be settled by humans.

China.text: Its shoreline spans four seas: the Bohai, the Yellow, the East China and the South China seas.
China.evidence: China's shoreline spans the Bohai Sea, Yellow Sea, East China Sea, and South China Sea, all part of the Pacific Ocean.
